Introduction-to-Blockchain(A-short-guide.content:
Blockchain

Blockchain in simple words is a distributed(decentralized) digital ledger(block) which contains records of various transactions
The transactions are recorded in various computers(also called nodes) so that the data can’t be manipulated easily.
In simple words, we can think of Blockchain as linked list of blocks with each blocks containing:

Data(like transactions)
Timestamp
hash of the previous block(link)
Note: Each Block also contains a lot more stuffs like metadata, Merkle root etc on the deeper level.


This creates a chain of block which is why it is called blockchain


Hashing


One of the major part of blockchain is hash value/hashing. It is a process of converting data to a fixed length output known as hash.  Blockchain technologies(like bitcoin) mostly use SHA-256 hash algorithm. SHA-256 hash algorithm provides a fixed output of 256 bits(64 hex characters), no matter how much the input size is.


Just a little change in input changes the output by a huge margin.


Example: Hashing the text Hello, Blockchain





Now if we just change the letter B to lowercase it’ll result in a huge difference as shown below:





In the case of bitcoin, every Blockchain is hashed using SHA-256 twice(double SHA-256). It is also used in Consensus Mechanism and Merkle Tree which we’ll learn later


Hashing not only helps in encrypting the data but also helps in linking the blocks together by their hash value.


Merkle Tree


In blockchain, there are lots and lots of transactions which happen in a short range of time and verifying it can be very hard. That’s where Merkle Tree or Hash Tree comes in. It is a binary tree structure which is used in blockchain to efficiently and securely verify large sets of data.


To understand more about the usecase of Merkle tree, let’s imagine a block with thousands of transactions, to prove that the transaction exists we need to go through every possible transaction. But with Merkle tree, by going through just a few hashes we can verify the transaction.


Structure of Merkle Tree

Leaf Nodes: Hash of each individual transaction
Intermediate Nodes: Pairwise combination of Hash
Merkle Root: The final single hash at the top i.e the root of the tree



Example:

Let’s say we have 4 transactions: T1, T2, T3 and T4
**Step 1: Hash each transaction

H1=hash(T1)
H2=hash(T2)
H3=hash(T3)
H4=hash(T4)

Step 2: Combine and hash the pairs

H12=hash(H1+H2)
H34=hash(H3+H4)

Step 3: Finally the Merkle Root

Merkle Root=hash(H12+H34)

So the tree, looks like:




Verifying a Merkle Tree

Let’s say we want to prove that T3 exists, for that we don’t have to go through all the hash, We just need H4(sibling of H3) and H12 i.e the other side of the tree
Then we can calculate Root as:

 
H34=hash(H3+H4)
Root=hash(H12+H34)

If the Root matches with the Merkle Root, we can say that T3 is in the block header.



Consensus Mechanism

A consensus mechanism is a method by which all the nodes(i.e computers) in a decentralized blockchain network agree on a single version of the truth, like which transactions are valid or which block gets added next.
To understand it, think of it like a group of people agreeing on what to write as an answer for the question or what to write in a segment, without a central authority
In decentralized systems, consensus mechanism is needed because there is no central authority and all the nodes must find a way to agree on:

Which transactions are valid
Who gets to add the next block
Preventing frauds and double-transaction


Common Consensus Mechanism

Proof of Work - Used by Bitcoin

Nodes compete to solve a complex mathematical problem (usually trying to find the optimal hash) and the first one to solve it gets to add a block and also earns a reward. This is what bitcoin-mining is.


Proof of Stake- Used by Ethereum 2.0

Validators are choosen to create the next block based on how much crypto they stake(lock up as a guarantee)
The more you stake, the higher your chance of being selected.




Note: There are various other consensus mechanism but I’ve only included two popular ones


Consensus Mechanism are the backbone of blockchain as without them there would be various conflict and anomalies and people would lose trust in the decentralized environment.

Summary

In this blog, we explored the foundational concepts of blockchain technology. We started by understanding what a blockchain is and how it maintains a secure, decentralized ledger. We then looked into hashing, which ensures data integrity, followed by the Merkle Tree structure that makes transaction verification efficient. Finally, we discussed consensus mechanisms like Proof of Work, which enable distributed nodes to agree on the state of the blockchain without needing a central authority.
Note from me: I’m currently on my journey of learning Web3 and blockchain development. This blog is part of my effort to understand the core concepts by explaining them in my own words. I’m still a beginner, so there may be mistakes. If you found any mistake please let me know
